Unified Two-Year Rent Allowance: Owners Who Haven't Signed Acquisition Letters Also Benefit

The government announced today that regardless of which option owners choose after selling their titles — including receiving cash only, receiving cash and then joining the "Special Sale Scheme," "flat-for-flat," or ultimately being unable to select a suitable unit under the "Special Sale Scheme" — they can receive a two-year rental allowance until 21 December 2027. The arrangement also applies to owners who have yet to sign the "Letter of Acceptance of Acquisition Offer."

As for owners participating in the "Special Sale Scheme," if the intake date of the unit is after 21 December 2027, the foundation will continue to disburse the rental allowance. The government stated that, considering owners generally need three months to renovate their new homes, owners' eligibility for the rental allowance will be maintained until three months from the date of the assignment of the newly purchased unit, after which the next instalment of the rental allowance will cease.

Cheuk Wing-hing: Listening to Concerns and Putting 'Compassion First' to Optimise Arrangements

Deputy Chief Secretary for Administration Cheuk Wing-hing said on a radio programme that residents and legislators had raised concerns about the original arrangements, including the inability to identify a unit immediately after selling their titles, the inability to select a suitable unit after joining the scheme, and the inability to terminate their existing tenancy. After listening to the views and giving them due consideration, the authorities decided to "put compassion first" and optimise the rental arrangements, providing greater flexibility for residents.

Previously Indicated That Owners Unable to Select Units Would Only Receive Rent Allowance Until Acquisition Payment Was Received

In December 2025, the government announced it would provide a rental allowance of HK$150,000 per year to owners of Wang Fuk Court, disbursed half-yearly in instalments of HK$75,000 each. However, after the long-term housing arrangement plan was announced in February, some briefing teams told residents that they would have to move out of transitional housing within 30 days of accepting the acquisition, and that the allowance would stop immediately upon receipt of payment, sparking concerns.

On 13 March, the government issued a statement to "clarify inaccurate reports," stating that the 30-day move-out was not a hard deadline, and that if an owner sold the title and received cash without joining the "Special Sale Scheme," the rental allowance would be disbursed until the relevant funds were credited; if they joined the scheme, the allowance would be disbursed until the intake date of the relevant subsidised housing unit.

Earlier there were further media reports that some residents were told by briefing teams that even if they participated in the "Special Sale Scheme," failing to complete unit selection by September would be treated as not participating, and the rental allowance would cease. The government said on Monday (the 13th) that if an owner was unable to purchase a unit under the "Special Sale Scheme," the allowance would be disbursed until the acquisition payment was credited — only to backtrack today (the 17th), stating that a two-year rental allowance would be uniformly provided.
